batch.title: WOCAT practice sheets: findings a rule kept
batch.notes: Findings taken from WOCAT practice sheets (forms filled in by practitioners). A rule kept each one because the sheet's comment explains how the practice works. This random sample checks that rule. Approve = right to keep. Reject = should not have been kept; I set it aside after reading your answers. The AI's suggested call shows under the buttons; it is a suggestion only.

units.citation: WOCAT (2026). Integrated Land Management for Gully Erosion Control through Gabions and Rock Check Dams in Guri Gaab Village. WOCAT SLM Technologies Database, Technology 7778 (Somalia). Compiler: ABDULLAHI ABDULKADIR.
units.quote: - downstream_siltation: value +2 — comment: Sediment transport downstream decreased as sediments are trapped upstream by gabion walls and check dams, reducing siltation in downstream agricultural fields and water bodies.

relationship.outcome_raw: WOCAT impacts_offsite.downstream_siltation rated +2 on the −3…+3 scale (right label 'decreased'); compiler: Sediment transport downstream decreased as sediments are trapped upstream by gabion walls and check dams, reducing siltation in downstream agricultural fields and water bodies.

units.question: The 2026 WOCAT sheet on gabions and rock check dams in a Somali gully rates downstream silting as reduced (+2 of 3), because sediment is trapped behind the walls and dams. We recorded it as a moderate gain in sediment trapped by runoff collection structures. Looks right: the sheet names the mechanism. Approve keeps it. Reject changes no rating; the water-table row for low-income countries just loses one paper. AI's view: The sheet's comment directly explains the siltation rating (sediment trapped behind check dams).

units.citation: WOCAT (2012). Vallerani System. WOCAT SLM Technologies Database, Technology 1528 (Burkina Faso). Compiler: Sabina Galli Vallerani.
units.quote: - water_quantity: value +2 — comment: With each rain, each micro basin can collect up to 1.200l of water. Each hectare collects an average of 360.000 liter of rain, runoff included. Collected in the micro basin, the water has enough time to infiltrate in the soil profile and eventually in the water table. Local people assert that after the implementation of the Technology, the water level in the wells has raised.

units.question: The 2012 WOCAT sheet on the Vallerani micro-basins (Burkina Faso) rates water quantity as increased (+2 of 3): each basin holds up to 1,200 litres per rain, water soaks in, and locals say well levels rose. We recorded a moderate cut in water shortage. Looks right. Approve keeps it. Reject: water-table recharge for water harvesting rises from moderate to strong, for the whole practice and for small in-field basins, because this rating is lower than the rest. AI's view: The comment gives the infiltration mechanism and reported well-level rise, matching the rating.

units.question: The 2014 WOCAT sheet on fenced area enclosures (Tanzania) rates water quantity as increased (+2 of 3), with only the note 'reduction in unproductive loss of green and blue water'. We recorded it as a moderate cut in water shortage from natural regrowth. The note is vague: it does not say more water reached wells, streams or people. Approve keeps it. Reject: water-table recharge for forest restoration drops from moderate to slight (3 papers to 2). AI's view: The one-line comment does not clearly show more usable water, yet this finding sets a headline rating resting on only three papers.

relationship.outcome_raw: WOCAT impacts_ecological_water.water_quantity rated +2 on the −3…+3 scale (right label 'increased'); compiler: They are used to capture and retain rainwater.

units.question: The 2022 WOCAT sheet on stone lines (Tunisia) rates water quantity as increased (+2 of 3), saying only that they 'capture and retain rainwater'. We recorded a moderate cut in water shortage. That is a slight stretch: stone lines hold water in the field soil, not in wells or ponds people draw on. Not counted in any rating today, so Reject changes no rating. Approve keeps it; Reject sets it aside. AI's view: The sheet supports more water retained; the stretch to water supply is minor and it moves no rating.

units.citation: WOCAT (2019). Broadleaf Plantations, Assisted Tree Regeneration and Fodder Nurseries for Sustainable Forest Management. WOCAT SLM Technologies Database, Technology 5243 (India). Compiler: Jaclyn Bandy.
units.quote: - fire_risk: value +3 — comment: The forest intervention area is protected by the villagers from anthropogenic and wild fires, therefore the forest has rehabilitated more quickly and has a lower risk of burning due to improved green vegetation cover and less flammable pine needle accumulation. In the case of pine forests, pine needles are a major source of fuel for fire and the removal of buildup remains a major challenge for the land users.

In the case of pine forests, pine needles are a major source of fuel for fire and the removal of buildup remains a major challenge for the land users.

units.question: The 2019 WOCAT sheet on broadleaf planting and assisted regrowth (India) rates fire risk as strongly reduced (+3 of 3): villagers guard the forest, green cover improved and less pine needle litter builds up. We recorded strong protection from fire. Looks right. Approve keeps it. Reject: forest restoration protection from fire stays moderate but confidence falls from high to medium (3 papers to 2). AI's view: The comment names the mechanisms (community fire protection, greener cover, less needle fuel).
